study.question: Can a pruned, target-independent mean-history residual retain the small validation gain of g1-r0008-mean_residual over g0 at lower measured cost, and does its content improve on an equal-active-capacity residual of the already available DIN summary?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: g1-r0008-mean_residual reached macro AUC 0.8307402933986681 versus g0 0.8301982212762624, adaptive incumbent replay 0.8307177422018418 and DIN reparameterization 0.8304973277289982. The 0.0000225511968263 mean-versus-adaptive difference is not evidence of superiority without repetition. Its 997.9541s wall cost and 45.3716s validation inference exceed g0 490.2476s and 37.6409s. Implementation inspection shows uniform event weights remove every dependence of the terminal update on evolving queries, event positions/keys, task identity and token content; narrow reads and task mixing are dead computations in this arm. A normalized low-rank transform of the unweighted historical item/action mean may complement g0 target-weighted summaries. Removing only the dead branch should retain that function at lower measured cost. The same-size DIN-summary replacement distinguishes additional mean content from an active residual parameterization, although input scale and gradient routing remain confounded. This is simplification and attribution of an existing local mechanism, with no originality claim.

nearest_work.difference: Primary archived arXiv:1706.06978v4 lines 250-274 inspected: candidate-conditioned local activation deliberately retains unnormalized weight magnitude. We preserve that inherited path and add the already tested, target-independent mean through a zero-start low-rank normalized residual. This is a field/four-task adaptation, not an exact DIN reproduction.

Pinned benchmark implementation 90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d lines 221-243 inspected: sequence encoding, query decoding and query boosting occur in each layer. This intervention deletes the terminal query route in the existing mean arm and keeps g0 representation construction. It does not implement HyFormer; original paper:hyformer detailed text is unavailable under the resolved archive, so original-method priority remains unverified.

Archived section 2.3 distinguishes stacked pooling/field interaction (including HiFormer) from layer-wise query exchange (including HyFormer). The pruned residual is a simple parallel summary added to the tower DIN input, not a new layer-wise unified architecture. Original HiFormer full paper was not available in the resolved source and is not treated as audited.

inherited_components: Complete g0-r0011-memory_joint_separate representation: raw static fields, signed DIN sum, five temporal bins, seven relation groups, linear-rank moments, relation/content parameter banks, factorized feedback-content maps, separate joint feedback memory, JointBlock and original four towers.
g1-r0008-mean_residual value_down [112,32], value_up [32,112], non-affine LayerNorm and zero-start output [112,112], with the ancestor initialization statements retained in identical order.

Historical residual constructor replay inside the inherited CPU RNG fork, followed by deletion of query/event/mixer modules before optimizer registration; no inherited reset after adding the residual.
Exact valid-history filtering, zero current action, masked IDs before Dice, null value only for all-empty history, four [B,1] probabilities and default four-BCE host loss.
study.proposed_difference: Replace terminal retrieval forward with FP32 uniform weights over valid history plus an empty-only zero null, followed by the original BF16 bmm and low-rank normalized residual. Preserve the four duplicate task summary shapes to reduce numerical changes. Remove registered event_projection/history_position/task_identity/read/after_read/final_norm and terminal-only field-match computation. Retired modules are constructed only to preserve retained initial tensors, then deleted; their methods never execute in forward. A second standalone arm changes only the residual summary to the existing global DIN sum. Analytic count at frozen widths: 19,712 active residual parameters above g0, 28,192 fewer than the unpruned ancestor; expected total 33,042,117, to be verified by host. Active mean and DIN arms have identical shapes and counts. No speed or quality measurement has yet been made for either new file.
predictions: Before any full training, host numerical preflight should confirm four finite probabilities, backward finiteness, zero residual on empty histories, and invariance to masked IDs/current action under frozen inputs. Compare shared inherited/retained initialized tensors with the archived ancestor at the same seed. Torch execution is unavailable in the coding environment; only syntax/AST/source checks were performed.

At identical retained weights, compact_mean should agree with the archived mean implementation up to numerical accumulation/kernel differences; exact real-arithmetic function equality does not imply BF16 bitwise equality. Host comparison should report maximum probability difference in FP32 and BF16; investigate a difference exceeding 1e-5 FP32 or 1e-3 BF16 before spending a complete training unit.

At the frozen seed, provisionally expect compact_mean macro AUC within 0.0001 and each task AUC within 0.0002 of g1-r0008-mean_residual, with lower measured train/inference cost. These are prospective diagnostic tolerances rather than changed selection rules. Selection remains highest validation macro AUC with frozen tie breakers.

If mean content is useful beyond a residual parameterization, compact_mean should exceed compact_din in paired macro AUC. Report macro Logloss and all task AUC/Logloss deltas against DIN baseline, g0, g1 source and both round-8 controls. Historical mean versus g0 improves click/cart/fav AUC but reduces buy AUC by approximately 0.00146048; a gain is not assumed uniform across tasks.

Use only existing host validation history slices empty, 1-16, 17-64 and >64 as exploratory diagnostics, with original per-task positives/negatives. The mean receipt contains 6,444/461,684/1,001,754/1,401,885 impressions respectively; the empty-history purchase count is only 13. Empty-history population predictions can change after retraining shared parameters despite the residual being structurally zero.

After attribution, paired validation repetitions rather than additional architecture search should test stability when the remaining resource and host phase permit. Repeated seed gains establish repeatability, not the causal need for adaptive queries.

Availability audit: task contract mentions validate_task.py, but resolving that reference returned Unknown authorized reference; no host validator was accessible. A standard-library recursive validation of the resolved study_schema, source syntax/import boundaries, CONFIG equality and allowed local evidence IDs passed. This missing interface is not experimental counterevidence. All queries, failed resolution and source checks consume preparation time; no local training or numerical execution was attempted.
falsifiers: Any nonfinite forward/backward result, dependence on masked/current-action inputs, changed inherited initialization, or violation of the source/feature contract invalidates the implementation; retain its charged failure and repair before comparison.

A substantial compact-versus-ancestor numerical discrepancy or performance shift outside the prospective tolerances contradicts the claimed preservation and requires diagnosing kernel, clipping or optimizer-order differences; do not attribute it to useful new information.

If the compact DIN-summary replacement matches or exceeds compact_mean in paired comparisons, complementary unweighted content is unsupported for this implementation; extra residual capacity or optimization remains sufficient.
If compact_mean does not exceed g0 at repeated validation seeds, the existing one-seed improvement is insufficient to establish repeatable source compatibility. Never treat source gains as additive.
If measured train/inference cost does not fall, do not claim efficiency from parameter removal or analytic FLOPs. Report the measured quality-cost tradeoff, even if quality is retained.

Earlier g1-r0006 adaptive prior failed to beat g0, no-prior did better, and both round-7 prior cells were worse than no-prior cells. These oppose a transferable field-match-prior explanation; pruning cannot establish g1 adaptive query/rotation mechanism support.
alternative_explanations: Single-seed winner selection, extensive shared-validation search and rare-label noise can explain small aggregate gains; no independent generalization estimate or significance claim is available.

An added nonlinear residual, normalization of the signed DIN magnitude, changed conditioning, shared embedding gradients or optimization could produce gains without additional useful history content. Equal-active-capacity DIN replacement addresses only part of this ambiguity.

Dropping exact-zero-gradient parameters changes optimizer parameter lists and potentially floating-point norm reductions under dense clipping. BF16 bmm layout changes can also perturb training; host numerical and initialization comparisons are necessary.

Mean pooling is target-independent only on this residual route; inherited DIN, relation masks, feedback memory, tokens and towers remain target-dependent. This does not show that the entire model needs no target conditioning.

Nominal parameter reductions are small relative to embeddings; runtime gains depend on removing query and event computations, which must be measured. Historical wall times are unmatched scheduling observations until host measurements confirm.

Official offline historical feedback can include immature delayed actions, and auxiliary labels match user/category/brand rather than ad-specific conversions. Nothing here validates production point-in-time behavior.
